questions.question: Guru Shashadhar Acharya was awarded the Padma Shri in 2020 for his contribution in which of the following fields?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**lok nritya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Padma Shri** is a **civilian award** in India, given to individuals who have made significant contributions in various fields such as **arts, literature, science, sports, social work, etc.**
 
• **Guru Shashadhar Acharya **is a renowned folk dance exponent from** Odisha, **known for his contribution to the promotion and preservation of traditional folk dances of the state.
 
• He was awarded with** padma shree in 2020**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vadya Yantra Vadan** refers to playing **musical instruments**. 
 
• Any device designed or modified to **produce melodies** is considered a musical instrument. 
 
• **Shastriya Nritya** refers to **classical dance forms.**
 
• **Bharatnatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, sattriya** are among the nine classical dance styles practiced in India.
 
• **Lok Nritya **refers to traditional** folk dances.**
 
• **Ghoomer, Kacchi Gori Chari, and Kalbelia** are a few of the most well-liked folk dances.
 
• **Hindustani Shastriya Gayan** refers to** classical music.**
 
• **Western art music**, which is generally distinguished from Western folk music or popular music traditions, is referred to as classical music.

questions.question: Which of the following musicians is associated with the instrument santoor?

__
 
• **Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma** is an **Indian classical musician** and a renowned **Santoor player.**
 
• Under the pseudonym **Shiv–Hari**, he worked as a music composer with Indian flautist **Hariprasad Chaurasia**, creating scores for popular Indian movies like **Faasle (1985), Chandni (1989), and Lamhe (1991).**

questions.question: What is the atomicity of Chlorine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diatomic.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorine** exists as a** diatomic molecule,** which means it consists of** two atoms of chlorine** joined by a **covalent bond.**
 
• The symbol for chlorine is Cl, and its atomic number is** 17, **which means it has **17 protons and 17 electrons **in its nucleus and shells, respectively.
 
• Chlorine is a** halogen**, and it is a **highly reactive nonmetal **that can form compounds with many other elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tetra-atomic** is a rare type of molecule that consists of **four atoms** of the same or different elements.
 
• Examples include s**ulfur tetrafluoride (SF4)** and **phosphorus tetraiodide (PI4).**
 
• **Poly-atomic molecules** are common in chemistry and include many organic compounds such as **glucose (C6H12O6) and DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid).**
 
• **Monoatomic**** **elements are rare and include **noble gases** such as **helium (He) and neon (Ne),** which exist as single atoms and **do not form** molecules with other atoms.

questions.question: How many elected members are there in the Legislative Assembly of Telangana till December 2022?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Legislative Assembly of Telangana** was formed in **2014 **after the state of Telangana was carved out of** Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• The term of the assembly i**s 5 years,** and the last state elections were held in **December 2018.**
 
• The assembly has a total of **119 seats.**
 
• The current Chief Minister of Telangana is **Revanth Reddy.****​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The youngest and **29th state** in the Union of India is Telangana.
 
• From **September 17, 1948, to November 1, 1956,** when it was combined with Andhra state to form Andhra Pradesh state, the Telangana region was a part of the **Hyderabad state.**
 
• Telangana was established when the** AP State Reorganization Bill **was approved by both chambers of Parliament, capping decades of campaigning for a separate State.
 
• It is said that the words "**Trilinga," or "Trilinga Desa," **which translate to "the country of the three lingas," are the source of both the language and the name "**Telangana."**

questions.question: In the year 2022, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare announced a National Suicide Prevention Strategy to reduce suicide mortality rate by ________ percent by 2030.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** announced the **National Suicide Prevention Strategy** in **2022** with the aim of reducing the suicide mortality rate by **10% by 2030.**
 
• Suicide is a major public health concern in India, with the country accounting for **17.8% of global suicide deaths **in 2019.
 
• The National Suicide Prevention Strategy aims to address the risk factors associated with suicide, such as** mental health issues, substance abuse, and social isolation,** through a multi-sectoral approach involving healthcare, education, and community-based interventions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suicide prevention** is a priority area for the government of India, and several initiatives have been launched in recent years to address this issue.
 
• These include the establishment of a **national helpline, training of healthcare professionals** in suicide prevention, and **community-based interventions.**
 
• The** World Health Organization** (WHO) states that although suicide is a major public health concern in India, it can be avoided with **prompt, evidence-based interventions.**
 
• One of the** Sustainable Development Goals (SDG3.4.2)** of the UN asks member nations to strive toward a **one-third reduction** in suicide rates worldwide by the year** 2030.**
 
• Suicide prevention is one of these goals.
 
• The** Mental HealthCare Act of 2017's** decriminalization of suicide and the establishment of India's first mental health toll-free helpline, **KIRAN**, are notable actions taken by the Indian government.​

questions.question: Who, being the Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Armed Forces, takes the salute of various regiments of the Armed Forces during the march-past on the occasion of Republic Day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **President of India** takes the **salute** during the march-past of various regiments of the **armed forces** on the occasion of **Republic Day.**
 
• The President of India is the** Commander-in-Chief **of the **Indian Armed Forces**, and hence, it is a tradition for him to take the salute during the Republic Day parade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** President of India** is elected by an** Electoral College **consisting of elected members of both houses of the **Parliament of India **and of the **Legislative Assemblies** of the States of India. 
 
• The **Defence Minister of India** is a member of the** Cabinet **and is responsible for the** Defence Ministry,** which is the ministry in charge of the armed forces of India.
 
• The **Prime Minister of India** is the leader of the **ruling party or coalition of parties** in the** Lok Sabha**, which is the lower house of the Parliament of India.
 
• The **Home Minister of India** is a member of the Cabinet and is responsible for the **Ministry of Home Affairs, **which is the ministry in charge of **internal security, law and order, and disaster management **in India.

questions.question: In which year did an English scientist named Michael Faraday discover benzene in illuminating gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1825.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Michael Faraday** discovered **benzene** in **illuminating gas **in the year **1825.**
 
• He collected compressed illuminating gas cylinders from the** pyrolysis of whale oil **and used them to extract benzene.
 
• This newly found l**iquid hydrogen **was dubbed a **bicarburet of hydrogen **by Faraday.
 
• German chemist** Eilhardt Mitscherlich** created benzene in **1834** by heating benzoic acid and lime.
 
• **A.W. von Hofmann**, a German chemist, separated benzene from coal tar in **1845.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Benzene **is a** colorless, highly flammable liquid** with a **sweet odor.**
 
• It is an important industrial chemical used in the production of various chemicals, including** plastics, synthetic fibers, rubbers, dyes, detergents, and pharmaceuticals.**

questions.question: In the later Vedic period, which of the following varnas were mainly involved in farming, animal husbandry and trade?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaishya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vaishyas **were the **merchant class** in ancient India and were mainly involved in **agriculture, trade, and commerce.**
 
• They were considered the **backbone of the economy** as they were responsible for** producing and distributing goods.**
 
• They were employed in **trade, agriculture, and pastoral work,** as well as in productive labor.
 
• Their way of life required** learning, selflessness, and almsgiving.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kshatriyas** were the **warrior class.**
 
• **They **were responsible for **protecting the kingdom** and** maintaining law and order.**
 
• **Brahmins **were the **priestly class.**
 
• **They **were responsible for performing **religious rituals** and** imparting knowledge.**
 
• **Shudras **were the **labor class.**
 
• **They **were responsible for **manual labor.**

questions.question: Identify the meaning of continentality.

options.text: Very hot during winters and very cold during summers
Very hot during summers and very cold during winters
Very hot during summers and lots of rain
Very cold during winters and not hot during summers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Very hot during summers and very cold during winters.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Continentality** refers to the **degree of temperature **variation within a landmass.
 
• Continentality is influenced by factors such as **latitude, altitude, ocean currents, and prevailing winds.**
 
• Continental climates are often found in the interior regions of large landmasses, such as **North America and Eurasia.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polar climates** are found in regions near the Earth's poles, while** tropical wet climates** are found in regions near the equator.
 
• **Monsoon climates** are found in regions that experience seasonal winds, such as southern Asia and parts of Africa.

questions.question: Who introduced the Zamindari Settlement as a measure of land revenue administration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Cornwallis.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** introduced the **Zamindari Settlement** in **1793 **as a measure of** land revenue administration **in British India.
 
• The Zamindari Settlement was a system of** land revenue collection** where the **East India Company **granted the zamindars (landlords) the right to collect revenue from the peasants in exchange for a **fixed amount of revenue** paid to the Company.
 
• The system was criticized for its** exploitation of peasants** by the **zamindars** and for perpetuating the feudal system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Lytton** introduced the infamous **Vernacular Press Act in 1878,** which curbed the freedom of the press in India and led to widespread protests.
 
• **Lord Curzon** was known for his administrative reforms in India, including the** partition of Bengal in 1905**, which sparked nationalist movements.
 
• **Lord Wellesley** was the **Governor-General of India** from **1798 to 1805** and is known for his** expansionist policies and the Subsidiary Alliance** system, which made Indian states dependent on the British.
 
• **Lord Cornwallis **was also responsible for introducing the **Permanent Settlement in Bengal,** which fixed the revenue to be paid by landowners to the Company, but led to the impoverishment of the peasants.

questions.question: The Indian Constitution originally consisted of ________ Articles.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**395.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Constitution originally consisted of **395 articles.**
 
• This number has since been amended several times, and currently the Indian Constitution has **448 articles.**
 
• Important sections of the Indian Constitution,** legislatures, executive branches, schedules, constitutional bodies, statutory bodies, fundamental rights,** and more are covered in each set of articles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Constitution is the** longest written constitution **of any sovereign country in the world.
 
• It was adopted on** November 26, 1949**, and came into effect on **January 26, 1950.**
 
• The Constitution originally had **22 parts**, but this number has since been revised to** 25 parts.**
 
• The Constitution also includes **12 schedules,** which contain various lists and tables related to important topics such as** languages, territories, and elections.**

questions.question: Which cells, also called neurilemma cells, are the main glial cells in the PNS and play an essential role in the survival and functions of neurons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Schwann cells.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Schwann cells** are the main glial cells in the **PNS.**
 
• They provide **myelin sheath** around the axons of neurons, which helps in faster **conduction of nerve impulses.**
 
• Schwann cells also play a crucial role in the **regeneration of damaged axons.**
 
• They are also involved in the maintenance of the **ionic environment **around the neurons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bipolar cells** are specialized neurons found in the **retina of the eye, **which help in** transmitting signals **from** photoreceptor cells** to ganglion cells
 
• **Ganglion cells** are the output neurons of the **retina**, which **transmit visual information** to the brain via the optic nerve.
 
• **Photoreceptor cells** are specialized cells found in the **retina of the eye, **which help in detecting light and converting it into **neural signals.**

questions.question: According to dietary guidelines recommended by physicians, the RDA for cholesterol intake in healthy adults and children over four years of age. (RDA) is ________ mg/day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**300.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **recommended daily intake of cholesterol **for adults and children over four years of age, according to the guidelines provided by healthcare professionals, is** RDA 300mg/day.**
 
• Cholesterol is an essential component of cell membranes and is also involved in the production of** hormones, vitamin D, and bile acids.**
 
• High levels of cholesterol in the blood can increase the risk of **heart disease and stroke.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cholesterol **is a** type of fat **that is produced by the** liver** and is also found in certain foods such as** meat, dairy products, and eggs.**
 
• **HDL (high-density lipoprotein)** cholesterol is often referred to as** "good" cholesterol** as it helps to remove excess cholesterol from the blood and carry it back to the liver for processing.
 
• **LDL (low-density lipoprotein)** cholesterol is often referred to as **"bad" cholesterol** as it can build up in the arteries and increase the risk of heart disease and stroke.
 
• **Eating a healthy diet, exercising regularly, and maintaining a healthy weight** can all help to reduce cholesterol levels and lower the risk of heart disease and stroke.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the characteristics of the new agricultural strategy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Use of organic manures.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The use of organic manures is **not** one of the characteristics of the new agricultural strategy.
 
• The following are the **characteristics** of the new agricultural strategy:
 
• **Use of chemical fertilisers:**
 
 
• The new agricultural strategy promotes the use of chemical fertilisers to **increase crop yield and improve soil fertility.**
 
• Chemical fertilisers provide **essential nutrients** to plants and help in their growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Use of hybrid seeds:**
 
 
• The new agricultural strategy emphasizes the use of hybrid seeds that are genetically engineered to **resist pests and diseases, tolerate adverse weather conditions, and enhance crop yield.**
 
 
 
• **Extensive irrigation:**
 
 
• The new agricultural strategy encourages the adoption of** extensive irrigation techniques **to ensure the availability of water for crops throughout the year.
 
• Irrigation helps in reducing the dependence on rainfall and mitigating the** impact of droughts.**
 
 
 
• **Mechanization:**
 
 
• The new agricultural strategy promotes the use of** modern farm machinery and equipment **that can perform various farm operations efficiently and effectively.
 
• Mechanization helps in reducing the** labor requirement and increasing productivity.**
 
 
 
• **Use of organic manures:**
 
 
• Organic manures are **natural fertilizers** that are derived from plant and animal sources.
 
• They are rich in** nutrients** and help in improving **soil health and fertility.**
 
• However, the new agricultural strategy does not emphasize the use of organic manures as they are** not **as effective as chemical fertilisers in increasing crop yield and productivity.
 
 
 
• **Use of chemical pesticides:**
 
 
• **​** The new agricultural strategy also promotes the use of chemical pesticides to **control pests and diseases** that can damage crops and reduce yield.
 
• However, excessive use of chemical pesticides can lead to **environmental pollution and health hazards. **
 
• Therefore, the new agricultural strategy emphasizes the judicious use of chemical pesticides and encourages the adoption of **integrated pest management practices.**

questions.question: Who among the following is a Nobel laureate, also known as the father of micro finance systems?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

• **Raghuram Rajan** is an Indian economist who served as the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India** from** 2013 to 2016**.
 
 
• He is known for his work on** financial regulation and macroeconomics.**
 
 
 
• **Sandra Rothenberg** is an **American professor and researcher **who is known for her work on corporate **social responsibility and sustainability.**
 
 
• **​**She has written several books and articles on these topics.

questions.question: In ________, Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the partition of Bengal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Curzon** was the **Viceroy of India **from** 1899 to 1905 **and he announced the** partition of Bengal in 1905.**
 
• The partition of Bengal was a British colonial policy that aimed to weaken the** nationalist movement in India **by dividing Bengal into two provinces, one **Hindu-majority **and the other **Muslim-majority.**
 
• The partition was widely opposed by **Indian nationalists**, who saw it as a deliberate attempt to divide and rule the country.
 
• The partition was eventually revoked in **1911**, due to sustained protests and political pressure from **Indian nationalists.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In order to deny Indians the right to self-governance, the** Lord Curzon's Calcutta Corporation Act of 1899** increased the number of nominated officials while decreasing the number of elected legislatures.
 
• After** 28 Corporation** members quit in protest, the Corporation was reorganized as a government department, with the majority of its employees being English and Anglo-Indian.
